lines.text: This soldier kept fighting World War II for 29 years after it ended.
Hiroo Onoda was a Japanese soldier sent to a Philippine island in 1944.
His orders were simple: never surrender.
In 1945, the war ended. But Onoda never got the message.
Planes dropped leaflets saying the war was over. He thought it was an enemy trick.
His friends gave up or died, until he was alone.
He lived in the jungle for decades, surviving on coconuts and bananas.
In 1974, a young traveler named Norio Suzuki found him. Onoda still refused to leave.
He said he would only stop if his own commander ordered it.
So Japan found his old commander, now a bookseller, and flew him to the island.
He finally gave the order, and Onoda surrendered after 29 years.
He wasn't hiding from the war. He was just still loyal to it.
